what: ResMed makes devices for sleep apnoea and respiratory conditions: the masks and flow generators used in continuous positive airway pressure therapy, plus software for the home medical equipment providers who supply them.
customers: Sleep apnoea patients through home medical equipment providers, hospitals, and the providers themselves who buy its software.
money: masks and consumable parts replaced regularly
software for home medical equipment providers
moat: Masks are personal and replaced every few months, so once a patient is fitted the recurring revenue follows, and the clinical data behind its devices is extensive.
risks: Weight-loss medicines could reduce the number of people developing sleep apnoea
Reimbursement decisions determine who gets a device paid for
Philips returning fully to the market after its recall would increase competition
opportunities: Operating margin of 33% and return on invested capital of 20%
Most people with sleep apnoea remain undiagnosed, so the market is far from saturated
Mask resupply gives recurring revenue that compounds with each new patient
watch: Device and mask revenue growth separately, and new patient starts.
